source_text:
Στρατευσώμεθα οὖν, ἄνδρες ἀδελφοί, μετὰ πάσης ἐκτενείας ἐν τοῖς ἀμώμοις προστώγμασιν αὐτοῦ.
κατανοήσωμεν τοὺς στρατευομένους τοῖς ἡγουμένοις ἡμῶν, πῶς εὐτάκτως, πῶς ἑκτικῶς, πῶς ὑποτεταγμένως ἐπιτελοῦσιν τὰ διατασσόμενα.
οὐ πάντες εἰσὶν ἔπαρχοι οὐδὲ χιλίαρχοι οὐδὲ ἑκατόνταρχαι οὐδὲ πεντηκόνταρχοι οὐδὲ τὸ καθεξῆς, ἀλλ’ ἕκαστος ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ τάγματι τὰ ἐπιτασσόμενα ὑπὸ τοῦ βασιλέως καὶ τῶν ἡγουμένων ἐπιτελεῖ.
οἱ μεγάλοι δίχα τῶν μικρῶν οὐ δύνανται εἶναι, οὔτε οἱ μικροὶ δίχα τῶν μεγάλων: σύγκρασίς τίς ἐστιν ἐν πᾶσιν, καὶ ἐν τούτοις χρῆσις.
λάβωμεν τὸ σῶμα ἡμῶν: ἡ κεφαλὴ δίχα τῶν ποδῶν οὐδέν ἐστιν, οὕτως οὐδὲ οἱ πόδες δίχα τῆς κεφαλῆς: τὰ δὲ ἐλάχιστα μέλη τοῦ σώματος ἡμῶν ἀναγκαῖα καὶ εὔχρηστά εἰσιν ὅλῳ τῷ σώμᾳτι: ἀλλὰ πάντα συνπνεῖ καὶ ὑποταγῇ μιᾷ χρῆται εἰς τὸ σώζεσθαι ὅλον τὸ σῶμα.
thought_title: The army and the body as models of ordered submission
orientation: Clement, writing from the Roman church to the Corinthian church, is urging the Corinthians to abandon their faction by showing how all ordered communities—an army and the human body—work together under one rule.
pass_a_gloss: Let us then serve as soldiers, men and brothers, with all earnestness in his blameless commandments. Let us consider those who serve as soldiers under our leaders, how orderly, how skillfully, how submissively they carry out the things commanded. Not all are prefects nor tribunes nor centurions nor commanders of fifty nor so on down, but each one in his own rank carries out the things commanded by the king and the leaders. The great without the small cannot exist, nor the small without the great: there is a certain blending in all things, and in these there is use. Let us take our body: the head without the feet is nothing, so also the feet without the head: but the least members of our body are necessary and useful to the whole body: but all breathe together and use one submission for the saving of the whole body.

choices.english: Let us then serve as soldiers
choices.why: The verb is a hortatory subjunctive; rendering it as 'serve as soldiers' preserves the military metaphor that Clement develops throughout the section.
The adjective 'blameless' modifies the commandments, not the soldiers; keeping it attached to 'commandments' preserves the source syntax.
rejected: in blameless obedience to his commandments

choices.why: The adverb describes trained, habitual competence; 'skillfully' captures the sense of practiced discipline without importing modern military jargon.
The adverb is cognate with the glossary term 'submission' (ὑποταγή); rendering it 'submissively' keeps the verbal link to the letter's key theme.

choices.term: σύγκρασίς τίς ἐστιν ἐν πᾶσιν, καὶ ἐν τούτοις χρῆσις
choices.english: there is a certain blending in all things, and in these there is use
choices.why: The two nouns are parallel and abstract; keeping them as nouns ('blending' and 'use') preserves the aphoristic quality of the Greek.
rejected: all things are mixed together, and these are useful

choices.why: The verb χρῆται takes the dative; rendering it as 'use one submission' keeps the same construction as the earlier 'in these there is use' and preserves the repetition of χρῆσις/χρῆται.

pass_b_english: So then, brothers, let us serve as soldiers with all earnestness in His blameless commandments.
Consider the soldiers who serve under our commanders. Notice how orderly they are, how skillfully they carry out their orders, how submissively they obey.
Not all of them are prefects or tribunes or centurions or commanders of fifty, and so on down the line. But each one, in his own rank, carries out what the king and the commanders order.
The great cannot exist without the small, nor the small without the great. There is a certain blending in all things, and in this blending there is purpose.

Take our own body. The head without the feet is nothing, and the feet without the head are nothing either. The smallest members of our body are necessary and useful to the whole body. All of them breathe together and submit to one rule, so that the whole body may be preserved.

polish.changed: Clarified who is being addressed and who gives orders, broke long sentences into natural modern rhythm, made the body analogy flow as one connected thought, and kept every claim and qualification intact.

last_rejected.why: The members make use of one submission; they do not submit to a rule.
last_rejected.fix: All breathe together and share one submission, so that the whole body may be preserved.
last_rejected.ruling: ὑποταγῇ μιᾷ χρῆται means 'use one subordination'; 'submit to one rule' is a natural idiomatic rendering conveying the same sense of unified subordination, not a meaning change.
